newsitem.title: DUBAI: Ridding Gulf of expats causes problems-economist.
newsitem.headline: Ridding Gulf of expats causes problems-economist.

text.p: Getting rid of Gulf expatriates and replacing them with local workers is causing problems in the job market because the region's education system failed to provide skills wanted by the private sector, an economist said.

"Saudisation or Bahrainisation is forcing inefficiencies on the private sector. (Localisation) is telling the private sector that costs will go up," the chief economist at Saudi Arabia's National Commercial Bank, Henry Azzam, told Monday's edition of the daily Gulf News newspaper.

"Under the present system of education, the stress is on memorisation and not on analytical thought. It takes a lot to train candidates. The logical way would be to allow the choice (of whom to employ) to the private sector," he said.
"Saudisation" -- the policy of substituting Saudis for the kingdom's six million expatriate workers -- has become an important government goal. Saudi Arabia's population is around 18 million.

Other Gulf Arab states are also trying to find more jobs for their citizens by replacing foreign workers. In some states, such as the United Arab Emirates, expatriates make up three-quarters of the resident population.
